Do not invent missing content for trust, secondary CTA, pricing values, form, or news sections.
Preserve a long-form rhythm: hero -> trust -> Seedream -> Seedance -> pricing -> testimonials -> footer.

Treat Seedream and Seedance as separate product story sections with consistent section header patterns but distinct content.
Mobile should collapse every multi-column pattern into a single-column stacked flow with full-width CTAs.
No form or news section should be added because the source content does not support them.

heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro—advanced foundation models from ByteDance for premium visual content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a premium dark split hero with the text block on the left and a cinematic layered media composition on the right. The right side should be a composed visual, not autoplay video: show a polished Seedream image canvas above a Seedance video preview card with timeline/waveform UI to communicate both products immediately. Keep the system orange-led on charcoal, with glass surfaces, subtle radial glow, and editorial spacing for a high-end enterprise AI feel.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a split-left hero that is content-first, then switch immediately to a trust-light utility strip instead of a second promotional block.
Use alternating dark band backgrounds across product sections to prevent visual monotony.
Present Seedream as a spotlight-plus-grid and Seedance as an accordion-with-visual to create distinct reading rhythms.
Move from expressive product storytelling into practical pricing cards, then into proof-led testimonials, then into a centered form for closure.
Keep CTA density strong in the hero and pricing, but lighter in proof sections to avoid repeated pressure.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro by ByteDance
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 for high-quality AI image generation and Seedance 1.5 Pro for cinematic AI video creation with synchronized audio, premium fidelity, and enterprise-ready creative output.

sections.backgroundTreatment: linear-gradient with orange radial glow and layered interface silhouettes
sections.designNote: PrimaryGoal: convert professional creative teams by clearly framing two flagship generative models. NarrativeMode: premium product revelation with technical confidence. TrustStrategy: credibility-through-capability since no badges or counts exist. VisualDominance: hero-message, so the left side must carry the headline, subheadline, and strong CTA while the right side shows a cinematic hybrid of image canvas, frame strips, waveform, and orange-lit UI panels. Keep the hero loud but disciplined, with a compact bullet value stack beneath the copy and no clutter.

Use a restrained capability-strip style instead of logos or customer metrics. Since trust assets are absent, convert this into a lightweight banner of product assurances: AI Image Generation, AI Video Generation with Audio, Multimodal Content Creation, Enterprise-ready AI infrastructure, and Transform ideas into visuals instantly. This section should feel useful rather than promotional, acting as a calm confidence bridge after the hero.

This section must open with Seedream 4.5 as the first flagship block, using a spotlight-plus-grid because it has 5 features and needs both depth and visual hierarchy. Give the image model a premium editorial treatment: large featured panel, then a 2-column feature grid for alignment, resolution, typography, composition, and structural fidelity. Immediately after, flip the rhythm for Seedance 1.5 Pro into an accordion-with-visual layout to create stronger contrast. That second block should feel more technical and kinetic, with audio-visual synchronization, lip-sync, camera control, and speed benefits folded into expandable rows beside a dynamic preview. Adjacent product blocks must not share the same visual pattern.

Even though the source content has no why-techjockey points, preserve this section as a short enterprise-assurance grid if editorially needed, or compress it into a subtle separator panel. Keep it functional, not salesy, and use it to reinforce platform confidence, procurement simplicity, and enterprise suitability without repeating the hero language.

Shift into a practical buying frame after the product storytelling. Present two clear pricing cards side by side, with Seedance 1.5 Pro visually emphasized because it has a starting price and audio-video differentiation. Keep the CTA as action-oriented but not aggressive: 'Get Quote' on both cards. Use a comparison-table feel rather than a generic SaaS pricing band, and include feature lists as decision support rather than marketing copy.

Because there are 5 testimonials, use a carousel instead of a simple grid. Let the testimonials function as proof-led validation, not as a loud sales block. Alternate between image-generation praise, video-generation praise, and evaluation/journey reassurance to show breadth. Keep visuals minimal with strong type contrast and dark cards, so the quotes feel credible and editorial.

Finish with a centered lead-capture card that feels like a refined close, not a forced funnel. Since the input has no form fields defined, make this a compact inquiry/demo card with a strong orange CTA aligned to the hero language. Keep the card floating on a darker field with soft glow edges, so the final conversion moment feels premium and focused.

Only use this as a low-prominence footer-adjacent strip if needed; the source has no news/logos. If rendered, convert it into a subtle moving credibility band or keep it visually quiet so it does not compete with the form. This should not become a promotional distraction.

blueprint.designPersonality: A dark, cinematic AI marketplace page with an orange-first brand identity, polished glass surfaces, and a sophisticated split narrative that makes Seedream and Seedance feel like two flagship creative engines under one premium system.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a cinematic dark hero visual with layered abstract AI shells, floating output previews, and orange-lit interface panels. Show one side as a high-end image canvas and the other as a video timeline / waveform / frame strip hybrid. Keep visuals glossy and enterprise-grade, with subtle glow around active states and no purple accents.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and needs a reduced size to preserve balance in a split-layout hero while still feeling premium and bold.

colours.colourReason: Brand primary is the required hero background and primary CTA color, so the page uses Techjockey’s deep charcoal base with the brand orange as the only strong accent. This creates a dark, premium AI identity while staying fully tied to the provided brand palette.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-column hero with logo lockup above a large headline, short supporting paragraph, and a compact bullet list of value props. Content is left-aligned on desktop, with strong vertical hierarchy and minimal visual clutter.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Long-form landing page rhythm: hero, lead capture/form block, then stacked product/feature sections. Sections are separated by clear vertical spacing rather than heavy decoration, with repeated header-to-features patterns.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Functional, flat content cards/forms rather than decorative cards. Uses bordered or lightly elevated panels for lead capture and feature grouping, with restrained styling and no glass/motion emphasis.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA is singular and action-oriented in the hero. Secondary conversion is handled through a prominent form-based CTA section. Section-level CTAs can appear as simple text/button actions inside feature blocks.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No clear pricing pattern present in the reference structure.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in the provided HTML; assume a standard low-prominence footer if needed, with minimal conversion focus.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the visible structure. Brand/logo placement is used in the hero, while the page relies primarily on typography and lists rather than large imagery, galleries, or videos.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Each product section follows a consistent pattern: label, headline, short description, then a feature list with concise title-description pairs. Sections are modular and repeatable, suitable for stacked comparison or sequential storytelling.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form block placed directly after the hero. Form is framed as a separate conversion module with a strong headline, hidden tracking fields, and a dense input structure intended for lead capture.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, conversion-first presentation with no visible motion system in the provided markup. If animated, keep transitions subtle and non-distracting.
designNotes: Prioritize clear hierarchy over visual ornament.
Use modular stacked sections for multiple offerings.
Keep CTAs prominent but limited in number.
Use whitespace and typography to separate content regions.
This reference supports a clean B2B landing page system rather than a highly interactive marketing experience.

blueprint.additionalInstructions: use dark theme for entire page

mustHaveMoments: Dark-theme hero with a strong headline, short supporting copy, and one primary CTA above the fold
Clear product separation between Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro with distinct use cases
Feature-led proof blocks emphasizing multimodal capability, resolution, typographic quality, audio-video sync, and speed
Testimonials placed early enough to reduce hesitation and validate enterprise use
Pricing or quote section framed as consultation-led rather than transactional
Persistent conversion path through repeated demo/request-quote CTAs
Low-friction footer with secondary reassurance and navigation only
avoidPatterns: Avoid bright, playful, or overly decorative visuals that weaken the enterprise-grade perception
Avoid cluttered layouts with too many media elements competing with the message
Avoid a form-first hero that interrupts product understanding before value is established
Avoid generic AI buzzword stacking without concrete capability proof
Avoid heavy motion, glass effects, or flashy gradients that reduce clarity in dark mode
Avoid equal-weight treatment of image and video offerings; keep the primary product narrative centered and the second as a strong supporting pillar
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is best approached as a lead-generation landing page for solution-aware professionals who already understand AI creation but need confidence in product quality and enterprise suitability. The content is highly product-centric, so the page should lead with a premium, message-forward hero, then quickly substantiate value through feature detail, testimonials, and quote/demo CTAs. A testimonial-first trust strategy fits the lack of logo or badge data while leveraging the provided quotes to reduce risk. Because the input requests a dark theme and the audience is professional, the visual system should feel premium, efficient, and restrained, with balanced density and a split hero that supports clear scanning and strong conversion.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
